one_line_contribution: It measures whether a reflection meta-prompt — the instruction that tells an LLM how to turn failure traces into prompt edits — transfers to held-out task domains, and how that held-out benefit scales with the number K of source tasks the meta-prompt was searched over; i.e. it ports the classical meta-learning 'meta-overfitting shrinks with task diversity' curve onto a natural-language meta-parameter, with a Pareto crossover-budget framing.
closest_prior_work: PromptBreeder (Fernando et al., 2023) is the direct threat and the proposal is right that it never evaluates an evolved mutation-prompt on a held-out task — but that concedes that the artifact, the self-referential outer loop, and the search operator are all already established, and what remains is an evaluation protocol plus a sweep whose direction (more source tasks -> less meta-overfitting) is known a priori from MAML-era task-diversity results the proposal itself cites. An AC will read the delta as 'existing method, new measurement, expected sign'. Worse, the Related Work omits the nearest neighbour for *textual cross-task transfer of how-to-improve knowledge*: the experience-distillation line (ExpeL-style insight extraction from a training task set applied to held-out tasks; Agent Workflow Memory-style induced-procedure reuse). Those already do cross-task natural-language transfer with held-out evaluation and some already ablate how much source experience is needed; the proposal must say why a reflection meta-prompt is a different object rather than the same idea one level up. REMO is cited and correctly distinguished (single benchmark, no held-out domain, no K sweep), which shows the authors can do this — they just did not do it for the closest line.
strongest_objection: The central object of the paper can be produced under the null, and the design does not have the resolution to rule that out. Three interlocking problems. (i) By the authors' own Risk Factor 1, each of the 20 meta-candidates is scored by averaging noisy 60-rollout inner runs, so the outer argmax may be selecting noise; the K-curve is then 3 noise-selected meta-prompts per level. (ii) Falsifiable Prediction (b) — 'the source-minus-held-out gap shrinks by at least half from K=1 to K=8' — is close to mechanically guaranteed even under a pure null on transfer, because the in-sample term is an argmax over 20 candidates scored on K tasks: winner's-curse inflation of the source-task gain falls as K grows and the outer selection is regularized by averaging, so the gap shrinks with K while held-out gain stays flat at zero. Making 'the meta-generalization gap' the headline object therefore builds a confirmatory result into the arithmetic. (iii) Power. The primary held-out contrast is described as n=30 paired observations (6 targets x 5 seeds) detecting 1.5 points at 80%, but the stated analysis clusters the bootstrap on target task — with 6 clusters the effective n for a transfer contrast is 6, not 30, and between-task variance in transfer gain is almost certainly larger than within-task seed variance. This is the same pseudo-replication the proposal explicitly guards against at the meta level and then reintroduces at the task level. The consequence is that the predicted +1 to +3 at K=4 versus +2 to +5 at K=8 is not separable by this design, so the monotone-in-K claim — the whole paper — will come back with intervals too wide to support it, and the fallback 'clean negative result' is then not clean either: it is under-powered, not null.
what_would_fix_it: Demote the gap and promote held-out gain to the sole primary endpoint, since only the held-out term is confound-free (the gap inherits the K-dependent winner's-curse shrinkage). Run the treatment-free meta-null replicate at *every* K, not once, so the observed K-slope is tested against a null K-slope produced by seed variation alone — that single change turns the strongest objection into a measured control. Recompute power with target task as the unit: 6 clusters will not do it, so buy resolution by adding target tasks (10-12) rather than seeds, and raise outer replicates from 3 to at least 5 meta-prompts per K. Add the amortization analysis the Pareto framing implies but never states: the outer search costs on the order of 10^4-10^5 rollouts, so report how many downstream tasks must be optimized before it pays back against simply giving the cold start more budget. Finally, fix the compute accounting (see feasibility): held-out evaluation alone is 12 meta-prompts x 6 targets x 5 seeds x 300 rollouts ~= 108k rollouts, which already exceeds the stated '~100k inner rollouts total' before the ~108k of outer search, six baseline arms, the oracle searches, the noise floor and the portability replication — a ~3x underestimate of the binding constraint, which matters because the likely response (cut seeds) destroys the already-marginal power.
missing_baseline: Two. (1) Random, non-reflective meta-prompt mutations *selected on the same K source tasks* at matched outer budget. Baseline (iv) as written scores random mutations 'on nothing', which is an unselected control, so nothing in the plan separates the self-referential reflective outer loop from plain best-of-N selection over variants — the cheap method any reviewer would demand, and the one most likely to match K=8. (2) A non-meta transfer locus: warm-starting the inner run on the target with the best source-task instruction skeleton or demo bank. The research brief asks a proposal to choose among transferable units and justify the choice; the plan's alternatives (harvested rule list, hand-written practice meta-prompt) are all still meta-prompt-level artifacts, so a positive result shows the meta-prompt is *a* transfer locus, never that it is the right one. A total-compute-matched cold start (cold start given the outer-search budget as extra inner rollouts) is a third, weaker omission that the crossover-budget analysis only partly covers.
preprint_collision: The Preprint Collision Check field is empty — no queries, no dates, no venues, no statement that a search was performed. That is a weakness, not a neutral, in an area where the threatening work is months old. The Related Work does cite 2025 items (GEPA, REMO), so there is some recency awareness, and REMO in particular is the kind of hit a real search produces — but citing two recent papers is not a collision check, and the authors give no evidence they looked for the cluster REMO sits in. Concrete things they must search and report on: (a) 2025 follow-ups to PromptBreeder on self-referential / evolved mutation prompts, especially any that evaluate an evolved mutation prompt off-task; (b) the active 2025 cluster on cross-run 'optimizer memory' / experience reuse layered on GEPA, TextGrad and DSPy — REMO is one member and it is implausible that it is the only one; (c) the experience-distillation line (ExpeL, Agent Workflow Memory and successors), which already distills natural-language lessons from a set of training tasks and evaluates on held-out ones, and which the proposal does not cite at all. I cannot name a preprint that makes exactly this claim — searched-meta-prompt held-out gain as a function of source-task count — and the specific K-sweep may well be unclaimed; but the authors have not established that, and under the brief's own standard an unsearched novelty claim should cost them.
